bingd.

{{greeting}}

Thanks for giving bingd. a go. I am Suraj, and at the moment I am the entire team, so this is genuinely me typing.

I built it because I could never answer “what should I watch”. I had years of films in my head in no particular order, and every app that offered to help wanted me to decide whether something was a four or a four and a half. I cannot do that. But I can always tell you which of two films I liked more, and it turns out that if you answer that enough times you end up with a list that is actually yours.

Two honest things. It is early, so you will find rough edges. And bingd. gets much better once one person you already talk about films with is on it, because the feed and Group Picks have nothing to show until somebody is on the other end of them.

Group Picks is my favourite thing in here, for what it is worth. You choose who is watching tonight and it finds the things you can all agree on.

If something is confusing, if you love something, or if the thing you went looking for is not there, just hit reply. It comes straight to me and I read every one.

— Suraj
Founder, bingd.
my profile on bingd.
 

A few things worth trying

Follow me

It gives you one person in your feed straight away, and I would like to see what you are watching.

Open my profile

Bring one person in

Nearly everything here needs a second person. This link is your own profile the way a stranger sees it, install button and all, so it is something you can forward as it stands.

See your profile

For the proper invite, the one that connects the two of you automatically, open bingd. and tap Invite friends on your profile.

Rank what I am watching

The Wolf of Wall Street is my number one and people keep telling me that is a red flag. Rank it yourself and tell me I am wrong.

Open the title

Whichever of those you try, tell me how it went. Replies come to me.
